Item: Choose how many slot packs to buy
What was wrong / what it is: The cart showed a quantity but there was no way to change it — the number was read-only, so buying two Premium ad packs meant adding the same item twice.
Fix / What was built: A minus/plus stepper on each cart line, backed by a new PATCH /api/cart. The line total, the slot count and the order total all move as it changes, and it survives a reload.
Why: Asked for directly: a way to set the quantity of slots from the cart.
Verified: 7/7 in the browser: 1 -> 3 slots EUR 100, 2 -> 6 slots EUR 200, 3 -> 9 slots EUR 300, back down, persisted

Item: MONEY BUG: paid for two packs, received one pack's slots
What was wrong / what it is: /api/cart/add already incremented quantity when the same pack was added twice, and the cart charged price x quantity — but provisioning read only the pack's own slot count. Two Premium ad packs took EUR 200 and granted 3 slots instead of 6. Nothing surfaced it: cart, order and PayPal charge were all correct; only the entitlement was short.
Fix / What was built: Fixed at the shared function so every payment rail is covered at once. The maths moved to lib/slot-count.ts, which imports nothing, so the guard script exercises the real function rather than a copy.
Why: This was live and reachable without the new stepper — anyone clicking Add to cart twice hit it.
Verified: 15 assertions incl. junk input falling back to one slot, never zero

Item: Quantity cannot be used to reprice a cart
What was wrong / what it is: A new write endpoint on the cart is a way to change what is charged if it trusts the client.
Fix / What was built: Only the quantity is writable — the price stays whatever the server set when the item was added. The line is looked up scoped to the caller's own active cart, so another buyer's id is simply not found. Capped at 25 per line because provisioning writes one row per slot.
Why: This is the money path.
Verified: 13/13 API assertions: validation, ownership, anonymous refused, client-sent price ignored, PayPal total tracks quantity

Item: Time remaining on every paid placement card
What was wrong / what it is: Side banners had a countdown; ad and featured-asset cards showed only a Created date. So the one thing a seller needs to act on — that a placement is about to stop — was the one thing not on the card.
Fix / What was built: The existing pill was lifted into a shared component and used on all three, rather than writing a second and third copy that would drift. Under seven days it turns red — the same threshold the profile's 'expiring soon' banner uses, so the two can never disagree.
Why: Asked for directly: show how long is left on each card.
Verified: Verified as a creator across ads, featured assets and side banners; 6d renders red, 13d/27d orange

Item: Countdown broke across three lines
What was wrong / what it is: On the one ad card that also shows clicks and views, the pill wrapped onto three lines. A countdown split over three lines is not a countdown.
Fix / What was built: The pill no longer wraps, and both card meta rows wrap as rows instead of crushing their children.
Why: Found while verifying the feature, not reported.
Verified: Measured every pill's rendered height: all single-line

Item: Seeded ads had no end date, hiding the feature
What was wrong / what it is: The local seed created ads with no endDate, so every seeded ad card read 'no end date'. A real ad always inherits its slot's end date, so the harness disagreed with production — and would have hidden exactly this feature from anyone testing it.
Fix / What was built: Seeded dates now span the states worth seeing: 60d, 21d, 14d and 3d.
Why: A harness that disagrees with production hides the bugs you built it to catch.
Verified: Reseeded and re-verified end to end

Item: FiveCrux's own coupon system, off Tebex
What was wrong / what it is: Coupons were handed to Tebex. The Apply button applied the code to a throwaway EMPTY basket just to hear whether Tebex liked it, and could not report the discount at all — the store required a buyer login before Tebex could price anything. The cart said 'PayPal shows the discounted total': the buyer had to commit to paying to learn what they saved.
Fix / What was built: Coupons are ours again and the amount is on screen before they commit. The scope and creator-ownership logic already existed in an orphaned file; rather than write a third implementation it is back in service as ONE validator used by both the Apply button and the PayPal order route.
Why: Asked for directly: take the coupon system off Tebex and build our own, end to end.
Verified: 23 assertions against a real throwaway database, 10 live API, 7 in the browser

Item: MONEY BUG: a single-use coupon was unlimited
What was wrong / what it is: Nothing ever wrote a coupon redemption or incremented usedCount — only the refund path decremented them. So maxUses and perUserLimit read counters that were permanently zero: a one-use coupon could be used any number of times, by everyone, forever.
Fix / What was built: Redemptions are now booked when the order is actually paid, idempotently, so a webhook retry cannot burn a second use.
Why: Direct, unbounded loss with nothing in the product to signal it.
Verified: Test proves the limits now trip: valid on first use, refused after one paid order, and a retry does not double-count

Item: MONEY BUG: creators were paid nothing on PayPal sales
What was wrong / what it is: A creator code's redemption row is where the creator's COMMISSION is recorded, and it was only ever written inside the Tebex checkout's finalizeBasket. When payment moved to PayPal nothing took that over — so every PayPal sale through a creator code paid the creator zero.
Fix / What was built: The commission travels on the order payload and is booked when the order is paid. Deliberately the figure agreed when the order was PRICED, not recomputed at capture, which would silently pay a different rate if the code changed in between.
Why: Found while fixing the identical hole in coupons — the same missing mechanism, one caller over.
Verified: Test asserts the row is written, the commission lands on it, usedCount rises, and a retry pays once

Item: Coupon scope was not enforced
What was wrong / what it is: An 'Ad Slots' coupon could discount a featured-slot purchase sitting in the same cart, because nothing checked what the coupon was scoped to.
Fix / What was built: Scope matching is enforced, and a plain creator's coupon still cannot reach another seller's products or FiveCrux's own placements.
Why: The scope field was authorable in the admin form and did nothing.
Verified: Tested: 'Ad Slots' coupon discounts only the ad slot; refused on a cart with none

Item: A flat coupon now comes off once, not per line
What was wrong / what it is: Nothing defined how a flat 'EUR 10 off' should apply to a multi-item cart.
Fix / What was built: Off the matching subtotal ONCE — EUR 10 off a five-item cart is 10, not 50 — matching what FiveCrux's own code did before Tebex. Clamped to the subtotal so a large flat coupon cannot produce a negative charge.
Why: Confirmed with the client before building.
Verified: Tested including a coupon larger than the cart

Item: Coupon codes could be enumerated
What was wrong / what it is: An unknown code and a switched-off code returned different messages, so the endpoint could be used to discover which codes exist.
Fix / What was built: Both answer the same way.
Why: Small, but it is a public endpoint with no rate limit in front of it.
Verified: Tested: identical response for both

Item: Removed the Tebex 'Coupon application rule' control
What was wrong / what it is: The admin form offered individual / basket_before_sales / basket_after_sales. It was a Tebex setting FiveCrux's own discount code never read, so all three options did exactly the same thing.
Fix / What was built: Control removed. The column stays (NOT NULL) so no migration is needed.
Why: A control that promises behaviour it does not deliver is worse than no control.
Verified: tsc + lint clean

Item: Deleted a second, contradictory coupon path
What was wrong / what it is: /api/cart/tebex-checkout, /api/cart/tebex-continue and finalizeBasket were still deployed and still applied coupons the Tebex way. Nothing had called them since the PayPal switch.
Fix / What was built: All three deleted.
Why: Two live code paths disagreeing about how coupons work is exactly the drift that caused this batch.
Verified: grep confirms no caller; tsc clean

Item: CRITICAL: every sitemap URL was malformed
What was wrong / what it is: Public URLs were built from NEXTAUTH_URL — an authentication variable doing SEO's job. In production it carries a trailing slash and the code appended another, so all 161 sitemap URLs came out as https://www.fivecrux.com//scripts. Every one 308-redirects: Bing and Google were handed 161 redirects instead of 161 pages.
Fix / What was built: lib/seo.ts is now the single source of truth: one origin, a slash-collapsing canonicalUrl(), and NEXTAUTH_URL explicitly not consulted.
Why: Found by auditing the live site, not reported.
Verified: Production sitemap: 161 malformed -> 169 clean, 0 double slashes, sampled URLs all 200

Item: CRITICAL: the fallback domain serves nothing
What was wrong / what it is: The base URL fell back to https://fivecrux.com — the apex, which resolves to a parking IP and answers nothing over HTTPS. The site only serves on www. Any deploy without NEXTAUTH_URL would have published a sitemap of dead links.
Fix / What was built: The canonical host is now the one that actually serves, set in code.
Why: Silent: the app cannot see that its own canonical host is unreachable.
Verified: Both hostnames probed; report now checks this on every run

Item: CRITICAL: Bing was watching a hostname that serves nothing
What was wrong / what it is: The verified Bing property was https://fivecrux.com/ — the dead apex. Nothing FiveCrux did could ever show up there. It also had ZERO sitemaps submitted, so Bing had never been handed the catalogue at all.
Fix / What was built: Added and verified https://www.fivecrux.com/ via Bing's API, and submitted the sitemap. The ownership token is committed in code rather than left to an env var, so verification survives a deploy instead of depending on a dashboard step — which is how the wrong host came to be verified.
Why: Client asked for the Bing account to be connected and used.
Verified: Bing API: www property VERIFIED, sitemap Status=Success, 169 urls crawled

Item: The sitemap claimed everything changed today
What was wrong / what it is: Every static route carried lastModified: new Date(), so the whole file said 'changed today' on every rebuild. A crawler that checks twice learns the field is noise and stops reading it.
Fix / What was built: Static entries carry a fixed date; listings carry their real updatedAt; category dates track their newest listing.
Why: An honest lastmod is the whole point of the field.
Verified: Verified in the generated sitemap

Item: Category pages were missing from the sitemap
What was wrong / what it is: The pages most likely to rank for terms like 'fivem maps' were never offered to a crawler.
Fix / What was built: Added, along with /marketplace. A database failure now returns the static routes rather than nothing.
Why: These are the highest-intent pages on the site.
Verified: Present in the live sitemap

Item: robots.txt was letting crawlers waste budget
What was wrong / what it is: Only /admin and /api were disallowed, so /profile, /cart and /edit-products were crawlable. No canonical host declared.
Fix / What was built: Driven by the same NOINDEX_PREFIXES list the app uses, and declares `host` so the apex and www are not read as two sites.
Why: A crawler spending its budget on /cart is not spending it on a listing.
Verified: Live robots.txt checked

Item: No canonical tags, Open Graph or site-level schema
What was wrong / what it is: There were no canonical tags anywhere — which, with a live www/apex split, is how duplicate content starts. The only structured data was per-product; nothing tied the brand together as an entity.
Fix / What was built: Canonical, metadataBase and per-page Open Graph, plus Organization and WebSite JSON-LD with a SearchAction on every page.
Why: metadataBase also stops Next resolving social previews against the Vercel preview alias instead of the real domain.
Verified: Live homepage carries canonical, msvalidate.01, og:title, Organization and WebSite

Item: Nothing told AI assistants what the site is
What was wrong / what it is: No llms.txt, no agent instructions. An assistant asked about FiveM assets had nothing to read but the rendered pages.
Fix / What was built: /llms.txt and /AGENTS.md: what the site is, when to reach for it, when NOT to, the read-only endpoints, and the things to get right (listings belong to creators; quote the listing's own currency; never tell someone they won a giveaway). robots.txt also names eleven AI crawlers explicitly — an opt-in signal, since it grants nothing '*' does not already.
Why: This is how the site gets recommended by an assistant rather than only found by a search engine.
Verified: Both live and returning 200. AGENTS.md needed a forced add — .gitignore excludes *.md, which would have kept a public asset out of the deploy

Item: IndexNow: stop waiting for Bing to come back
What was wrong / what it is: Nothing told search engines when something changed. A new marketplace has almost no crawl budget — Bing decides how often to return based on how often it found something new, which is a slow loop from zero.
Fix / What was built: Key file, submitter and a daily Vercel cron. Sitemap-driven, so there is one list of what is public rather than two.
Why: Fastest available way to get 169 pages looked at.
Verified: Submitted 169 urls live, HTTP 202 accepted

Item: Nothing could measure any of this
What was wrong / what it is: Everything above was invisible from the repo: the only way to see whether it landed was to open Bing's dashboard by hand.
Fix / What was built: lib/bing.ts wraps Bing's Webmaster API, and `npm run seo:report` prints what Bing holds plus what the live site serves — hostnames, files, sitemap health, on-page tags, verification, feeds, traffic. Read-only, and exits non-zero so it can gate a deploy later.
Why: It is what found every SEO item in this batch.
Verified: Before: 10 problems. After: 0.
